name: Great Northwoods 290-point
description: Rubric adapted from the Great Northwoods Sales judges' criteria for use in Relii. Faithful 290-point structure across six categories. Each item is worth 10 points and carries sub-criteria guidance so the scorer can make and explain itemized deductions. Items tagged voice-only are skipped for text sessions and the total is pro-rated. Each item also lists the scenario types it belongs to.

meta.source: Great Northwoods Judges' Criteria (OS_Resources/Relii/Great-Northwoods-Judges-Criteria rubric.pdf), mapped to Relii scenario types per Tom Banta, June 14, 2026.
meta.status: Confirmed by Tom. Great Northwoods is the rubric. It is mapped into two scenario types via the per-item 'meetings' tags.
meta.scoring_note: For a text session, omit voice-only items and pro-rate: text max equals the scenario's voice plus video max minus its voice-only points.
meta.format_note: Relii role plays are a webcam call where the student is on camera and the AI persona is voice-only. Physical in-person actions (handshake, business card exchange) are not applicable and are not scored.

discovery.name: Discovery-Close
discovery.objective: Secure the follow-up meeting with Jordan.

presentation.name: Presentation-Close
presentation.objective: Secure a business agreement (the risk-free trial order).

items.label: Professional opening
items.guidance: Professional greeting and stating first and last name clearly, politeness. Penalize failure to state first and last name. Handshake, fist bump, and business card exchange are not applicable to the remote AI format and are not scored; allocate the points across greeting, self-identification, and politeness.

items.label: Effectively builds rapport
items.guidance: Connects with the prospect and finds an area of commonality, builds credibility. Eye contact is assessed only in voice plus video sessions; in text, score the rapport-building content.

items.label: Displays organized meeting prep
items.guidance: States the purpose of the meeting, reviews or presents an agenda, asks the customer for feedback on the agenda or topics.

items.label: Uncovers the purchasing process
items.guidance: Uncovers length of the purchasing process and any constraints: approval process, budget, timing.

items.label: Determines relevant facts about current practices
items.guidance: Confirms current target markets or customers served, solicits feedback on current or past products and services purchased, identifies current suppliers of similar products, identifies order frequency.

items.label: Uncovers criteria for purchasing new products
items.guidance: Surfaces the decision criteria the customer uses when buying new products or services.

items.label: Effectively uncovers the needs of the buyer
items.guidance: Asks engaging questions relevant to the customer's concerns, uncovers elements of the customer's strategy, and uncovers industry and market pressures facing the customer.

items.label: Increases awareness of opportunities and the total cost or impact of not changing
items.guidance: Helps the customer discover the loss (the total cost or impact) of not changing, understand the gains of changing, and begin thinking through possible solutions.

items.label: Sparks interest in hearing more about the product or service
items.guidance: Communicates how the product or service can address the problem or opportunity in an impactful way.

items.label: Summarizes needs and transitions to the presentation
items.guidance: Refers to the agenda, summarizes findings and progress, and asks the customer for feedback before moving into the presentation.

items.label: Organized presentation that is easy to follow
items.guidance: All information is relevant to a problem, opportunity, or the purchasing process; the presentation flows, adjusts to customer interest, and is not overly scripted.

items.label: Uses objective data to tell a story
items.guidance: Data and numbers are not just reported; specific examples show how the story is relevant to the customer.

items.label: Presents benefits tied to the problem, solution, or opportunity
items.guidance: Relates benefits clearly to the customer's problem, solution, or realized opportunity.

items.label: Effectively engages buyers with the product
items.guidance: Demonstrates product knowledge, shares interesting facts relevant to the customer, and presents creative ideas for using the product or service.

items.label: Summarizes and persuasively presents a reason to buy
items.guidance: Pulls the case together into a persuasive reason to buy.

items.label: Gauges interest in purchasing (soft close)
items.guidance: Uses open-ended questions to gauge purchase interest.

items.label: Asks for buyer feedback and solicits objections
items.guidance: Invites feedback and surfaces objections rather than avoiding them.

items.label: Asks an open-ended question before answering an objection
items.guidance: When an objection arises, asks an open-ended question to understand it before answering.

items.label: Effectively answers the objection
items.guidance: Answers the objection with relevant facts or product information.

items.label: Confirms the objection is no longer a concern
items.guidance: Asks a question to confirm the objection is resolved.

items.label: Directly asks for the business and suggests an order size
items.guidance: Directly asks for the business and proposes an order size.

items.label: Knowledgeable of price and discounting
items.guidance: Shows command of price and discounting when completing or presenting the order.

items.label: Prepared to complete the transaction
items.guidance: Provides clear next steps regardless of the customer's answer and gains commitment for follow-up.

items.label: Uses engaging professional visual or physical aids
items.guidance: Uses professional visual or physical aids. Requires the webcam (voice plus video); not scored in text.

items.label: Engages buyers with the presentation by asking questions
items.guidance: Keeps the buyer engaged by asking questions throughout.

items.label: Effective verbal communication skills
items.guidance: Appropriate business grammar and language, minimal slang, minimal filler words, no distracting verbal tics, not reliant on a script. Requires speech; not scored in text.

items.label: Appropriate non-verbal communication
items.guidance: No distracting behaviors or tics, not slouching, appropriate eye contact, no repetitive checking of phone or watch. Requires the webcam; not scored in text.

items.label: Professional dress and image
items.guidance: Professional dress and image that does not distract from the presentation. Requires the webcam; not scored in text.

items.label: Attitude and confidence
items.guidance: Enthusiasm shown through smiling, body language, voice tone and pace; confident in tone and behavior. Requires voice plus video; not scored in text.
